issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the solution expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This name/signature mismatch can confuse students: following the UML or the solution they will implement SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery to call addToStockIngredients, but the template does not contain that method, causing compilation errors or extra work to discover the correct method to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the UML and the solution. Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), or add a forwarding method addToStockIngredients that calls addItem. Ensure the template's Stock class includes addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) so students can follow the UML and implement SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery without compilation issues.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution implementation use the method name addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) to add a StockIngredient to the Stock, while the template Stock class provides the method addItem(StockIngredient). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (adding a StockIngredient to the Stock) can confuse students who are expected to map the UML and problem description to the starter code and final solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) so it matches the method name used in the problem UML and the solution. Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to consistently use addItem, but keeping the UML, template, and solution aligned will reduce student confusion.
